ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the industrial structure unfolds layer by layer from left to right. The pie chart on the left shows that this region has primary, secondary, and tertiary industries; the arrow points to the pie chart of the internal structure of agriculture in the middle, in which “planting industry” accounts for the vast majority, while forestry, animal husbandry, fishery, and agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, and fishery service industry account for relatively small proportions; then an arrow points to the pie chart of the internal structure of the planting industry on the right, in which “cotton” accounts for the vast majority, while grain and other crops account for relatively small proportions. Reasoning: The question asks about the most important locational advantage condition for agricultural production in this region, so one should grasp the dominant direction of agriculture in the figure. Agriculture in this region is dominated by the planting industry, and the planting industry is dominated by cotton, so the judgment should be made based on the locational requirements of cotton production. Cotton growth requires strong sunlight and long sunshine duration; good sunlight conditions are beneficial to cotton growth and the formation of quality, so the most important locational advantage condition for agricultural production in this region is sufficient sunlight.
